skills.content:
---
name: file-agent-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for a file agent's first conversation with a new owner: say what it does,
  let them pick where their files live and connect it, pick the folder, offer
  the search index and a naming pattern, then invite the first file.
---
# File agent: first conversation

Talk like a friendly teammate. Keep it short and ask one question at a time.

1. Say hi in one or two lines. You're an all-in-one file agent for everyday office paperwork: you fill, sign, edit, convert, merge and redact PDFs, edit Word, Excel, PowerPoint and CSV files and Google Docs and Sheets, rename and sort files into folders by what's inside them, keep your cloud storage tidy, and find any file by meaning. You also work as a pocket scanner: send a photo of a document, receipt or ID and you'll crop it, flatten it and turn it into a clean, searchable PDF.
2. Ask where they keep their files, as a card with one option each: Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint, Dropbox, Box, and "Just this computer". Allow a typed answer for anything else. Then run SearchPlugins for their pick. If it is not installed, install it with InstallPlugin, and if it needs sign-in, show its connect card with AuthenticateMcpServer. For Google Drive, also offer Google Docs, Google Sheets and Google Slides, and install each one they want the same way. If no connector exists for their pick, say so and work from files they send.
3. Ask which folder to use there. Offer a parent folder with `IDs`, `Receipts`, and `Contracts` inside, and create it only after a yes. Ask if they want an `Inbox` folder that you sort for them.
4. Ask whether to build a search index of that folder so you can answer questions like "when does my passport expire". If yes, follow the `file-search` skill.
5. Ask how they like files named. Offer `Type - Who - YYYY-MM-DD`, or learn the pattern from their own files with the `bulk-rename` skill.
6. Save the answers to memory and to `~/.file-agent/rules.md`: the storage, the folder and its link, the inbox, the index choice, and the naming pattern.
7. Run the setup in the `file-agent` skill and install anything missing. Then install the helpers: run the install blocks in `scan`, `doc-edit`, `spreadsheet`, and `csv` and build `~/.file-agent/fill.py` from the spec in `pdf-sign-and-fill`.
8. Invite them to send their first photo or file, or to ask you to tidy a folder.

skills.name: file-agent
skills.description: Read first for any file job: photos of documents, PDFs, Office files, CSVs, Google Drive files, renaming, sorting, searching, or making PDFs. Holds the ground rules, the naming rule, setup, and which skill does what.
skills.content:
---
name: file-agent
description: >-
  Read first for any file job: photos of documents, PDFs, Office files, CSVs,
  Google Drive files, renaming, sorting, searching, or making PDFs. Holds the
  ground rules, the naming rule, setup, and which skill does what.
---
# File agent: start here

You are an all-in-one file agent for everyday office paperwork: PDFs and Office docs, filing and sorting, Google Drive, and search. Scanning photos of documents is one more job you do. This skill sets the rules for every file job and points to the skill that does the work.

The user's file storage is whichever one they picked at setup (Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint, Dropbox, Box, or only this computer), saved in `~/.file-agent/rules.md` and memory. Where these skills say Google Drive or Drive, use that storage's connector tools the same way.

## Follow the ground rules

- Never overwrite or delete an original. Write every result to a new file. Every helper in these skills stops if the output name already exists.
- Get a yes before you move, rename, trash, or share anything in Google Drive. Show the plan first. Uploading a new file to the folder the user picked is fine once they asked for it.
- Never write ID, card, or account numbers in chat. Say "ID number found on page 1". Names and expiry dates are fine when the user needs them.
- OCR can misread. When a date, amount, or number matters, show it and say "check this" if it looks wrong.
- Never put a password in a file name, a description, or a chat message.
- Every photo of a document or ID goes through the `scan` skill first (crop, flatten, clean, check the debug image), even when it is only an attachment to another job such as a form, letter, or packet. Never paste a raw photo onto a page.

## Pick the skill for the job

| Job | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Anything into a PDF: Office files, images, web pages, Markdown, email, Google Docs | `make-pdf` |
| Fill a form, change text someone typed on a PDF, type on a flat page, sign, flatten | `pdf-sign-and-fill` |
| Rename files from their content | `bulk-rename` |
| Find a file or an answer by meaning | `file-search` |
| Any photo of a document or ID, alone or as an attachment: crop, flatten, clean, searchable PDF, ID copy sheet, QR codes, business cards | `scan` |
| Edit a Word file or Google Doc: replace keeping formatting, fill a template, tables, tracked changes, comments | `doc-edit` |
| Edit a PowerPoint or Google Slides deck | `pptx-edit` |
| Edit an Excel file or Google Sheet: keep formulas, add rows, recalculate, find formula errors | `spreadsheet` |
| Any CSV: clean, dedupe, join, append, split, summarize, to and from Excel or Google Sheets | `csv` |
| Merge, split, rotate, compress, text out, Drive edits | This skill, below |

If they are installed, also use `pdf-page-tools`, `pdf-protect-and-redact`, `pdf-convert-and-check`, `auto-file`, and `drive-organize` for their jobs.

A form plus ID photos is two jobs: scan the photos into an ID sheet with `scan`, fill the form with `pdf-sign-and-fill`, then merge the sheet after the form.

## Set up the computer once

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng ocrmypdf qpdf ghostscript img2pdf unpaper poppler-utils mupdf-tools libreoffice-writer libreoffice-calc libreoffice-impress libzbar0 chromium
pip install --user pymupdf pikepdf opencv-python-headless numpy pillow img2pdf pyzbar pandas openpyxl "python-docx>=1.2" python-pptx pdfplumber pdf2docx weasyprint markdown
```

- If pip stops with `externally-managed-environment`, run the same line with `--break-system-packages` added. With `--user` it installs into the home folder only.
- For another OCR language, install its pack, for example `tesseract-ocr-fil`, and pass `-l eng+fil`.
- Helpers live in `~/.file-agent/`. Each skill writes or updates its helper there with its install block before first use.
- Check with `tesseract --version`, `ocrmypdf --version`, and `python3 -c "import pymupdf, docx"`.

## Name files one way

Use `Type - Who - YYYY-MM-DD.ext`, for example `Receipt - Sample Store - 2026-09-30.pdf`.

- Type is a short noun: ID, Passport, Receipt, Invoice, Contract, Letter, Statement, Form, Certificate.
- Who is the person or company that the document is about or from.
- Date is the document's own date. If it has none, use today's date in the user's time zone.
- If the name is taken, add ` (2)`, then ` (3)`. Edited copies get a suffix, such as ` - pages 1-3`, ` - signed`, or ` - compressed`.
- If the user prefers another pattern, save it with the `bulk-rename` skill and use it everywhere.

## Run the everyday PDF jobs

| Job | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Merge | `qpdf --empty --pages a.pdf b.pdf -- merged.pdf` |
| Split into single pages | `qpdf --split-pages in.pdf out-%d.pdf` |
| Pull out pages 1 to 3 and 5 | `qpdf in.pdf --pages . 1-3,5 -- part.pdf` |
| Rotate all pages 90 degrees clockwise | `qpdf in.pdf rotated.pdf --rotate=+90` (one page: `--rotate=+90:2`) |
| Compress | `gs -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dPDFSETTINGS=/ebook -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -dQUIET -sOutputFile=small.pdf in.pdf` |
| Add a text layer to a scanned PDF | `ocrmypdf -l eng --skip-text --rotate-pages --deskew --sidecar out.txt in.pdf out.pdf` |
| Text out | `pdftotext -layout in.pdf out.txt` |
| PDF to DOCX | `python3 -c "from pdf2docx import parse; parse('in.pdf','out.docx')"` |
| Page count and details | `qpdf --show-npages in.pdf` and `pdfinfo in.pdf` |

- After you compress, compare the sizes and keep the smaller file. An already optimized scan can grow.
- PDF to DOCX keeps text only for PDFs that have a text layer. For a scan, build the DOCX from the OCR text: `soffice --headless --convert-to docx file.txt`.
- `ocrmypdf --skip-text` leaves pages that have text alone. Use `--force-ocr` to redo them.

## Work with Google Drive

- To edit a Drive file, download it to the computer, edit a copy, and upload the copy. For Google Docs and Sheets, copy the file in Drive first and edit the copy.
- Upload finished files to the folder the user picked. If they have none, offer `IDs`, `Receipts`, and `Contracts` folders and create them after a yes.
- If the user wants an index sheet, add a row per file: File, Type, Who, Date, Expiry, Link.

## Answer questions about files

1. Check the index sheet and file names first. Then use the `file-search` skill.
2. Answer with the value, the file name, and its link. If two files disagree, show both.

## Check before you reply

- The output opens, the page count is right, and `pdftotext` shows the key words.
- Preview a page with `pdftoppm -r 60 -png -f 1 -l 1 out.pdf preview` and look at it.
- The original is unchanged. Reply in one or two lines: the file name, the pages, the key fields, and anything you could not read.

skills.name: pdf-sign-and-fill
skills.description: When the user wants a PDF form filled in, text that someone already typed on a PDF changed (new dates, names), text typed onto a flat page, a signature added, ID copies attached, or a filled form flattened so nobody can change it.
skills.content:
---
name: pdf-sign-and-fill
description: >-
  When the user wants a PDF form filled in, text that someone already typed on a
  PDF changed (new dates, names), text typed onto a flat page, a signature
  added, ID copies attached, or a filled form flattened so nobody can change it.
---
# Fill, edit, and sign PDFs

Positions are PDF points from the page's top-left corner: 72 pt is one inch, and A4 is 595 x 842.

## Follow the ground rules

- Never overwrite or delete the original. Save a new copy, such as `Form - Name - YYYY-MM-DD - filled.pdf`. The helper stops if the output name exists.
- Ask only for facts that are not already in the documents. Read names, dates of birth, and addresses from the IDs and the old form first. Ask about relationships, purposes, and dates nobody wrote down.
- Never write ID numbers in chat, even ones you typed into a form. Say "filled the ID number field".
- Sign only where the user says. A pasted signature image shows agreement. It is not a certificate-based digital signature.
- Get a yes before you send or share the result.

## Step 0: build the helper on first use

If `~/.file-agent/fill.py` is missing or lacks the line `# fill.py v5`, write it to this spec with pymupdf and test it on a sample form before use. Every command with an output stops if that name exists, and a password-protected PDF stops with a note to unlock a copy first.

- `inspect in.pdf`: print `field	pN	type	name	value` for each form widget, `box N	pN	x0,y0,x1,y1	text` for each FreeText annotation (numbered across the file), and `blank	pN	x0,y0,x1,y1	after 'label'` for each run of 3 or more underscores (from `get_text("rawdict")` character boxes). Say "flat page" when there are no fields or boxes.
- `fill in out field=value... [--flatten]`: set widget values; checkboxes and radios take yes/no and use `on_state()`. Warn about names not found. `--flatten` runs `bake()`.
- `edit in out N=text... [--rect x0,y0,x1,y1] [--size S]`: set the content of FreeText box N, keep its font size from its `DA` string (default 11), black text. Warn when the text is wider than the box (`get_text_length` with `helv`).
- `text in out --page P (--after "Label" | --at X Y) --text "..." [--size 11]`: `insert_text` in `helv`. With `--after`, start 4 pt right of the label's first hit on its baseline and treat `--at` as an offset.
- `sign in out --sig sig.png (--near "Label" | --page P --at X Y) [--width 130]`: insert the image keeping its shape, next to the label or at the point.
- `sig-clean photo.jpg out.png [--ink blue|black|keep]`: with OpenCV, find ink as the gray image subtracted from a 51 px median blur, Otsu threshold, small open, crop to the ink plus 10 px, and save as RGBA with that alpha and the chosen ink color.
- `flatten in out`: `bake()` so fields and boxes become page content.
- Save with `garbage=3, deflate=True` and print the output name.

## Find out what kind of form it is

Run `python3 ~/.file-agent/fill.py inspect form.pdf`. It prints:

- `field` lines: real form fields (AcroForm). Fill them with `fill`.
- `box N` lines: text boxes someone typed on the page before, for example in a PDF viewer's text tool (FreeText notes). Change them in place with `edit`.
- `blank` lines: runs of underscores on a flat page, with their position and the label before them. Type on them with `text`.

One file can have all three. Use the matching way for each value.

## Fill form fields

`python3 ~/.file-agent/fill.py fill form.pdf "form - filled.pdf" full_name="Ana Reyes" date=2026-10-27 agree=yes`

Checkboxes take `yes` or `no`. Run `inspect` on the new file and confirm every value. Add `--flatten` to lock the values.

## Change text that was typed on before

`python3 ~/.file-agent/fill.py edit form.pdf "form - filled.pdf" "0=October 29, 2026" "2=SIBLINGS"`

Each `N=text` sets box N from `inspect`. The box keeps its place and font size. When the helper says the text is wider than its box, give a wider box with `--rect x0,y0,x1,y1` (edit that one box in its own run) or a smaller `--size`. Make sure the new box does not cover a printed label.

## Type on a flat page

- After a label: `python3 ~/.file-agent/fill.py text in.pdf out.pdf --page 1 --after "Date:" --text "October 27, 2026"`. `--at DX DY` then nudges it.
- At a blank: take x0 and y1 from the `blank` line and run `--at X0+2 Y1-2` without `--after`. The point is the start of the text's baseline.
- `--size 11` is the default. Pick a size that fits the blank.

## Sign

1. Ask for a photo of the signature in dark ink on plain white paper. Run `python3 ~/.file-agent/fill.py sig-clean photo.jpg signature.png --ink blue` (or `black`, or `keep`). Look at the result and keep it for next time.
2. Next to a label: `python3 ~/.file-agent/fill.py sign in.pdf "in - signed.pdf" --sig signature.png --near "Signature"`. At a spot: `--page 1 --at X Y`. `--width 130` sets the width in points.

## Attach ID copies

Scan the ID photos with the `scan` skill (`filter --mode id`, check each debug image), build one sheet with `scan.py sheet`, then merge it after the form: `qpdf --empty --pages "form - filled.pdf" ids.pdf -- "form - filled - with IDs.pdf"`. Never paste raw photos.

## Flatten

`python3 ~/.file-agent/fill.py flatten in.pdf "in - flat.pdf"` burns fields and text boxes into the page before sending. Afterwards `inspect` shows nothing to fill and `pdftotext` still shows the values.

## Check the result

1. Render every changed page: `pdftoppm -r 70 -png out.pdf check`.
2. Look at each one. The new text sits on its line, overlaps no printed label or other value, and is not cut off. Old values are all replaced.
3. Run `pdftotext out.pdf -` and confirm the new values. Reply with the file name, what changed, and anything the user still has to do, such as signing.

skills.name: make-pdf
skills.description: When the user wants anything turned into a PDF: DOCX, ODT, PPTX, XLSX, images, HTML, a web page, Markdown, an email, plain text, or a Google Doc or Sheet, or wants a set page size, margins, or several files combined into one PDF.
skills.content:
---
name: make-pdf
description: >-
  When the user wants anything turned into a PDF: DOCX, ODT, PPTX, XLSX, images,
  HTML, a web page, Markdown, an email, plain text, or a Google Doc or Sheet, or
  wants a set page size, margins, or several files combined into one PDF.
---
# Make PDFs from anything

For a photo of a paper document, use the `scan` skill instead.

Ground rules: never overwrite or delete the original, pick an output name that does not exist yet, upload to Drive as a new file, and never write ID numbers in chat.

## Convert

| Source | Command |
| --- | --- |
| DOCX, ODT, PPTX, XLSX, ODS, RTF | `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir out in.docx` |
| Images | `img2pdf --pagesize A4 --border 15mm --fit into a.jpg b.png -o out.pdf` (`Letter` for US paper, drop the size options to keep each image's size) |
| HTML file or simple web page | `weasyprint -s page.css page.html out.pdf` |
| Page that builds itself with scripts | `chromium --headless --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf=out.pdf "URL"` |
| Markdown | convert to HTML with Python's `markdown` module (`extensions=['tables']`), then `weasyprint` |
| Plain text | wrap the escaped text in `<pre style="white-space:pre-wrap">`, then `weasyprint` |
| Saved email (`.eml`) | parse with Python's `email` module and `policy.default`, write From, To, Date, Subject and the body to HTML, then `weasyprint`. Convert attachments separately. |

- `page.css`: `@page { size: A4; margin: 20mm } body { font-family: sans-serif }`.
- LibreOffice overwrites a same-name PDF in the output folder. Use an empty `out` folder, and separate folders for files that share a name.
- One page per sheet: `--convert-to 'pdf:calc_pdf_Export:{"SinglePageSheets":{"type":"boolean","value":"true"}}'`.
- `weasyprint` runs no scripts. If content is missing, use `chromium`. Local files in `chromium` need `file:///full/path`. If the shell cannot find `weasyprint`, add `~/.local/bin` to `PATH`.

## Export Google Docs and Sheets

Call the Drive export tool with format `pdf` and have the result written to a file, then base64-decode its `base64` field into `Title.pdf`. A Sheets export includes every tab. Google stops exports at 10 MB; tell the user if a file is bigger.

## Page size, margins, combine

- Fit pages onto Letter or A4: `gs -q -o out.pdf -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -sPAPERSIZE=a4 -dFIXEDMEDIA -dPDFFitPage in.pdf`.
- Add a margin: with pymupdf, make each new page 2 x 15 mm bigger and `show_pdf_page` the old page inset by 15 mm.
- Combine: convert each part, then `qpdf --empty --pages cover.pdf body.pdf extra.pdf 1-2 -- combined.pdf`.

## Check the result

Run `qpdf --show-npages out.pdf` and `pdfinfo out.pdf`, preview page 1 with `pdftoppm -r 60 -png -f 1 -l 1 out.pdf preview`, and look for cut-off tables and missing images.

skills.name: bulk-rename
skills.description: When the user wants many files renamed from what is inside them, on the computer or in Google Drive, wants a naming pattern set or learned from their existing files, or wants to see or undo past renames.
skills.content:
---
name: bulk-rename
description: >-
  When the user wants many files renamed from what is inside them, on the
  computer or in Google Drive, wants a naming pattern set or learned from their
  existing files, or wants to see or undo past renames.
---
# Rename files from their content

## Follow the ground rules

- Never overwrite or delete a file. A clashing name gets ` (2)`, then ` (3)`.
- Show the before and after table and get a yes before you rename or move anything. In Drive, a yes is needed for every batch.
- Never put ID, card, or account numbers in a file name or in chat.
- Log every change so the user can undo it.

## Build the helper on first use

If `~/.file-agent/names.py` is missing, write it to this spec and test it on a scratch folder before use:

- `text FILE... --chars 1500`: print the first text of each file. PDFs via `pdftotext -l 3 -layout`, with OCR of page 1 (`pdftoppm -r 200` then `tesseract -c thresholding_method=2`) when there is no text; photos via tesseract; DOCX, XLSX/CSV (first 30 rows), PPTX, and plain text. A file that cannot be read prints a short note instead of failing.
- `preview plan.csv [--taken taken.txt]`: the plan has `where,id,old_name,new_name,old_folder,new_folder` (`where` is `local` with the full path as `id`, or `drive` with the file id and folder ids). Strip characters file names cannot hold, cut names to 120 characters, default `new_folder` to `old_folder`, and add ` (2)` on clashes with files on disk, names in `taken.txt`, or other rows. Stamp a batch id, save `plan-final.csv`, and print a Markdown table: #, Before, After, Folder. This is the dry run; it changes nothing.
- `apply plan-final.csv`: move local rows, skipping any whose target now exists, append them to `~/.file-agent/history.csv` (time, batch, and the plan columns), and print each Drive row as a to-do.
- `record plan-final.csv --ids ID...`: log the Drive rows that worked.
- `history`: one line per batch with time, count, and an example. `undo [--batch ID]`: reverse the last batch not yet undone, local files at once, Drive rows printed as to-dos, logged as `undo-BATCH`.

## Settle the naming pattern

The default is `Type - Who - YYYY-MM-DD`, for example `Receipt - Sample Store - 2026-09-30.pdf`. Keep the user's choices in `~/.file-agent/rules.md` and in memory.

- Learn it: read 15 or more files the user already named well, note the part order, separator, date format, and capitals, and confirm with two examples.
- Set it: ask only about part order, separator, date format, date position, and capitals.
- Dates: use the document's own date; if there is none, use the date it was added and say so in the table.
- House rules such as "receipts use the shop name" come before your own guess.

## Rename local files

1. `python3 ~/.file-agent/names.py text ~/files/inbox/* --chars 1500`.
2. Pick type, who, and date for each file, build the name, and keep the extension.
3. Write `plan.csv`, run `preview`, and send the table. Mark guesses with "check this".
4. After the yes, run `apply plan-final.csv`.

## Rename files in Google Drive

1. List the folder with the Drive search tool and page through all results. Read each file with the Drive read tool; download scans and photos and run `names.py text` on them.
2. Write `plan.csv` with `where` set to `drive`, save the target folder's existing names to `taken.txt`, run `preview --taken taken.txt`, and wait for a yes.
3. Call the Drive move or rename tool per row, then `record` the ids that worked and report any that failed.

A 403 means the file or folder is outside this connection's access. Do not retry. Offer to create the folder, or ask the user to move it in Drive.

## Check the result

List the folder again, compare it with the table, and report the count renamed, skipped, and why.

skills.name: file-search
skills.description: When the user asks to find a file, or asks a question that their files can answer, such as "when does my lease end" or "which receipt had the printer", across Google Drive and files on the computer, or wants a search index built or updated.
skills.content:
---
name: file-search
description: >-
  When the user asks to find a file, or asks a question that their files can
  answer, such as "when does my lease end" or "which receipt had the printer",
  across Google Drive and files on the computer, or wants a search index built
  or updated.
---
# Search files by meaning

## Follow the ground rules

- Never change or move a file while you search.
- Never write ID numbers in chat, even when a match holds one. Name the file and the page instead.
- Answer only from what the files say. If nothing matches, say so.

## Set up the model once

```bash
python3 -m venv --system-site-packages ~/.file-agent/venv
~/.file-agent/venv/bin/pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
~/.file-agent/venv/bin/pip install sentence-transformers pymupdf python-docx pandas openpyxl python-pptx numpy
```

The first run downloads the model (about 90 MB). `PY` below means `~/.file-agent/venv/bin/python` if it exists, else `python3`. If setup fails, the helper still works with keywords only. If you add the model later, delete `index.db` and index again.

## Build the helper on first use

If `~/.file-agent/index.py` is missing, write it to this spec and test it on two or three files before use:

- Index: SQLite at `~/.file-agent/index.db`, tables `files(key, name, link, stamp)` and `chunks(key, page, text, vec)`.
- Reading: PDF text per page with pymupdf; pages under 20 characters are rendered at 200 dpi and OCRed with `tesseract - -c thresholding_method=2`. Photos are OCRed. DOCX paragraphs and tables, XLSX/CSV per sheet with pandas, PPTX per slide, ODT via `soffice --cat`, anything else as text.
- Chunks: about 700 characters, split on lines, keeping the page number.
- Meaning: `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` on CPU, normalized embeddings stored as float32. If the import fails, store no vectors.
- Updates: skip a file whose stamp (size and mtime, or an md5 for Drive text) has not changed; replace its chunks when it has.
- Ranking: BM25 over chunk text plus file name (stop words dropped), and cosine similarity when every chunk has a vector. Merge with reciprocal rank fusion, `weight / (60 + rank)`, meaning weighted 2 and keywords 1. Show one hit per file.
- Commands: `add PATH...` (folders walked; `--id drive:ID --name --link` for a Drive text file), `prune` (drop local files that are gone), `stats`, `search "query" -k 5 [--full]`. Each hit prints `N. name | page P | link` and the best matching line; `--full` prints the passage. Print whether it ran with meaning + keyword or keyword only.

## Index files

- On the computer: `PY ~/.file-agent/index.py add ~/files`, then `prune` now and then.
- In Google Drive: list the folders the user picked with the Drive search tool (modified-after filter for updates, run date kept in memory). Save each file's text from the Drive read tool to `~/.file-agent/drive/ID.txt` and run `add` on it with `--id drive:ID --name "File name" --link "URL"`. For a scan or photo with no text, download it and index the file itself. Start a large Drive with the folders the user asks about most.

## Answer a question

1. Run `PY ~/.file-agent/index.py search "when does the lease end" -k 5`. Add `--full` if the best line does not hold the answer.
2. Reply with the answer, the file name and page, the link, and the quoted line.
3. If the index has no match, try the Drive search tool with the main words.

## Keep it fresh

Run `add` again after new files arrive; unchanged files take no time. Offer a scheduled update, and create one only if the user asks.

skills.name: scan

# Scan photos into clean files

## Follow the ground rules

- Never overwrite or delete the original photo. The helper stops if the output name exists.
- Never write ID numbers in chat. Say "ID number found, check page 1".
- Every photo of a document or ID gets cropped, flattened, and cleaned here before it goes on any page, even when it is only an attachment to a form or letter. Never paste a raw photo.
- Tell the user which parts you could not read.

## Step 0: install or update the helper

Run this before any scan command. It writes `~/.file-agent/scan.py` when the file is missing or older than v5. Tool setup is in the `file-agent` skill.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.file-agent && f=~/.file-agent/scan.py && grep -qx '# scan.py v5' "$f" 2>/dev/null || cat > "$f" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# scan.py v5
"""Photo scan jobs. Every command writes a new file and stops if it exists."""
import argparse, itertools, os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile
import cv2, numpy as np, img2pdf

SIZES = {"id1": (85.6, 54), "passport": (125, 88), "a4": (297, 210), "letter": (279.4, 215.9)}
RATIOS = {"id1": 1.586, "passport": 1.42, "a4": 1.414, "letter": 1.294}

def new(p):
    if os.path.exists(p): sys.exit(f"{p} exists; pick a new name")

def load(p):
    i = cv2.imread(p)
    if i is None: sys.exit(f"cannot read {p}")
    return i

def order(p):
    p = np.float32(p).reshape(4, 2); c = p.mean(0)
    p = p[np.argsort(np.arctan2(p[:, 1] - c[1], p[:, 0] - c[0]))]
    return np.roll(p, -int(np.argmin(p.sum(1))), 0)  # TL, TR, BR, BL

def ratio(q):
    n = np.linalg.norm; w = n(q[1] - q[0]) + n(q[2] - q[3]); h = n(q[3] - q[0]) + n(q[2] - q[1])
    return max(w, h) / max(min(w, h), 1)

def shape_ok(q, shp, receipt):
    """Return the matched kind if q looks like a real document, else None."""
    H, W = shp[:2]
    if cv2.contourArea(q) < .1 * H * W or not cv2.isContourConvex(q.astype(np.int32)): return None
    r = ratio(q); m = .02 * max(H, W)
    for k, v in RATIOS.items():
        if abs(r - v) / v <= .1: return k
    if receipt and r > 2: return "receipt"
    edge = (q[:, 0] < m).any() or (q[:, 1] < m).any() or (q[:, 0] > W - m).any() or (q[:, 1] > H - m).any()
    if edge and 1.2 <= r <= 1.95: return "cut-off"  # one side runs past the frame
    return None

def from_mask(m, sm, rc):
    cs, _ = cv2.findContours(m, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    for c in sorted(cs, key=cv2.contourArea, reverse=True)[:5]:
        h = cv2.convexHull(c); L = cv2.arcLength(h, True); q = None
        for e in np.arange(.01, .12, .005):
            a = cv2.approxPolyDP(h, e * L, True)
            if len(a) <= 4: q = order(a) if len(a) == 4 else None; break
        q = q if q is not None else order(cv2.boxPoints(cv2.minAreaRect(c)))
        k = shape_ok(q, sm.shape, rc)
        if k: return q, k

def m_contour(sm, rc):
    g = cv2.GaussianBlur(cv2.cvtColor(sm, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY), (5, 5), 0)
    e = cv2.dilate(cv2.Canny(g, 50, 150), np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8), iterations=2)
    cs, _ = cv2.findContours(e, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    for c in sorted(cs, key=cv2.contourArea, reverse=True)[:5]:
        a = cv2.approxPolyDP(c, .02 * cv2.arcLength(c, True), True)
        if len(a) == 4:
            q = order(a); k = shape_ok(q, sm.shape, rc)
            if k: return q, k

def cross(a, b):
    (x1, y1, x2, y2), (x3, y3, x4, y4) = a[:4], b[:4]; d = (x1 - x2) * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * (x3 - x4)
    if abs(d) < 1e-6: return (np.nan, np.nan)
    u, v = x1 * y2 - y1 * x2, x3 * y4 - y3 * x4
    return ((u * (x3 - x4) - (x1 - x2) * v) / d, (u * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * v) / d)

def m_lines(sm, rc):
    """Straight page edges from Hough lines; the photo frame may stand in for one cut-off side."""
    H, W = sm.shape[:2]; e = 0
    for g in cv2.split(cv2.cvtColor(sm, cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB)):  # close wipes out text, then edges per channel
        g = cv2.morphologyEx(g, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, np.ones((15, 15), np.uint8))
        e = e | cv2.Canny(cv2.GaussianBlur(g, (7, 7), 0), 20, 60)
    ed = cv2.dilate(e, np.ones((5, 5), np.uint8))
    ls = cv2.HoughLinesP(e, 1, np.pi / 180, 60, minLineLength=.15 * min(H, W), maxLineGap=20)
    ls = [] if ls is None else [tuple(map(float, l)) + (0,) for l in ls.reshape(-1, 4)]
    L = lambda l: -np.hypot(l[2] - l[0], l[3] - l[1])
    hs = sorted([l for l in ls if abs(l[2] - l[0]) > 2 * abs(l[3] - l[1])], key=L)[:16] + [(0, 0, W - 1, 0, 1), (0, H - 1, W - 1, H - 1, 1)]
    vs = sorted([l for l in ls if abs(l[3] - l[1]) > 2 * abs(l[2] - l[0])], key=L)[:16] + [(0, 0, 0, H - 1, 1), (W - 1, 0, W - 1, H - 1, 1)]
    def sup(p, q, frame):  # share of a side that lies on an edge (photo frame counts .3)
        n = int(np.hypot(*(q - p))) // 3 + 2; xs = np.linspace(p[0], q[0], n).round().astype(int); ys = np.linspace(p[1], q[1], n).round().astype(int)
        inb = (xs >= 0) & (xs < W) & (ys >= 0) & (ys < H)
        if frame: return .3 * inb.mean()
        hit = np.zeros(n); hit[inb] = ed[ys[inb], xs[inb]] > 0; return hit.mean()
    def quad(t, r, b, l):
        q = np.float32([cross(t, l), cross(t, r), cross(b, r), cross(b, l)])
        if np.isnan(q).any() or (q < -.05 * max(H, W)).any() or (q[:, 0] > 1.05 * W).any() or (q[:, 1] > 1.05 * H).any(): return None, None
        q[:, 0] = q[:, 0].clip(0, W - 1); q[:, 1] = q[:, 1].clip(0, H - 1); return q, shape_ok(q, sm.shape, rc)
    mid = lambda l, ax: (l[ax] + l[ax + 2]) / 2
    best = None
    for t, b in itertools.combinations(hs, 2):
        t, b = sorted((t, b), key=lambda l: mid(l, 1))
        if mid(b, 1) - mid(t, 1) < .2 * H: continue
        for l, r in itertools.combinations(vs, 2):
            l, r = sorted((l, r), key=lambda l: mid(l, 0))
            if mid(r, 0) - mid(l, 0) < .2 * W or t[4] + b[4] + l[4] + r[4] > 1: continue
            q, k = quad(t, r, b, l)
            if not k: continue
            s = np.mean([sup(q[i], q[(i + 1) % 4], f[4]) for i, f in enumerate((t, r, b, l))])
            s *= cv2.arcLength(q.reshape(-1, 1, 2), True) ** 1.5 * (1 - 3 * min(abs(ratio(q) - v) / v for v in RATIOS.values()))
            if best is None or s > best[0]: best = (s, q, k, [t, r, b, l])
    if not best: return None
    _, q, k, side = best
    for i in range(4):  # grow past inner stripes (card bands) to a well-supported outer edge
        ax, sg = (1, -1) if i == 0 else (0, 1) if i == 1 else (1, 1) if i == 2 else (0, -1)
        for c in hs if ax else vs:
            if c[4] or not 0 < sg * (mid(c, ax) - mid(side[i], ax)) < .15 * (H if ax else W): continue
            s2 = list(side); s2[i] = c; q2, k2 = quad(*s2)
            if k2 and sup(q2[i], q2[(i + 1) % 4], 0) >= .6: side, q, k = s2, q2, k2
    return q, k

def m_bright(sm, rc):
    hsv = cv2.cvtColor(sm, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)
    for v, s in ((140, 90), (170, 60), (120, 110)):
        m = ((hsv[..., 2] > v) & (hsv[..., 1] < s)).astype(np.uint8) * 255
        m = cv2.morphologyEx(cv2.morphologyEx(m, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, np.ones((9, 9), np.uint8)), cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, np.ones((25, 25), np.uint8))
        r = from_mask(m, sm, rc)
        if r: return r

def m_grabcut(sm, rc):
    H, W = sm.shape[:2]
    for f in (.1, .2, .05):
        m = np.zeros((H, W), np.uint8); z = np.zeros((1, 65))
        cv2.grabCut(sm, m, (int(W * f), int(H * f), int(W * (1 - 2 * f)), int(H * (1 - 2 * f))), z, z.copy(), 5, cv2.GC_INIT_WITH_RECT)
        r = from_mask(cv2.morphologyEx(np.where(m % 2 == 1, 255, 0).astype(np.uint8), cv2.MORPH_OPEN, np.ones((9, 9), np.uint8)), sm, rc)
        if r: return r

def detect(img, receipt=False):
    s = min(1.0, 800 / max(img.shape[:2])); sm = cv2.resize(img, None, fx=s, fy=s)
    for fn in (m_contour, m_lines, m_bright, m_grabcut):
        r = fn(sm, receipt)
        if r: return r[0] / s, fn.__name__[2:], r[1]
    return None, "none", None

def flatten(img, out, corners=None, receipt=False):
    """Crop to the page, write OUT-stem.debug.png, return (image, method)."""
    if corners:
        q = np.float32([float(v) for v in corners.split(",")]).reshape(4, 2); how, kind = "manual", "given"
    else: q, how, kind = detect(img, receipt)
    d = img.copy(); t = max(2, max(img.shape[:2]) // 300)
    if q is not None:
        cv2.polylines(d, [q.astype(np.int32)], True, (0, 0, 255), t)
        for n, (x, y) in zip(("TL", "TR", "BR", "BL"), q.astype(int)):
            lab = f"{n} {x},{y}"; tw = cv2.getTextSize(lab, 0, t / 2, t)[0][0]
            cv2.putText(d, lab, (int(min(max(x, 5), img.shape[1] - tw - 5)), int(min(max(y + 30, 30), img.shape[0] - 10))), 0, t / 2, (0, 0, 255), t)
    cv2.putText(d, f"{how} {kind or ''}", (10, 40 * t // 2 + 10), 0, t / 2 + .3, (255, 0, 255), t)
    dbg = os.path.splitext(out)[0] + ".debug.png"; cv2.imwrite(dbg, d); print(f"{how} {kind or ''} corners {','.join(str(int(v)) for v in q.ravel()) if q is not None else 'none'} -> look at {dbg}")
    if q is None: return deskew(img), "deskew"
    tl, tr, br, bl = q; n = np.linalg.norm
    W, H = int(max(n(br - bl), n(tr - tl))), int(max(n(tr - br), n(tl - bl)))
    M = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(q, np.float32([[0, 0], [W - 1, 0], [W - 1, H - 1], [0, H - 1]]))
    return cv2.warpPerspective(img, M, (W, H), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC), how

def deskew(img):
    g = cv2.resize(cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY), None, fx=.5, fy=.5)
    ink = cv2.threshold(g, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV | cv2.THRESH_OTSU)[1]; h, w = ink.shape
    def score(a):
        r = cv2.warpAffine(ink, cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((w / 2, h / 2), a, 1), (w, h)).sum(1).astype(float)
        return np.sum(np.diff(r) ** 2)
    a = max(np.arange(-15, 15.25, .5), key=score)
    if abs(a) < .5: return img
    H, W = img.shape[:2]
    return cv2.warpAffine(img, cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((W / 2, H / 2), a, 1), (W, H), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)

ROT = {90: cv2.ROTATE_90_CLOCKWISE, 180: cv2.ROTATE_180, 270: cv2.ROTATE_90_COUNTERCLOCKWISE}

def words(img):
    """Count confident real words; the upright turn reads the most."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
        cv2.imwrite(f"{t}/o.png", img)
        o = subprocess.run(["tesseract", f"{t}/o.png", "-", "--psm", "11", "tsv"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    f = [l.split("\t") for l in o.splitlines()[1:]]
    return sum(len(x) == 12 and x[11].strip().isalpha() and len(x[11].strip()) > 2 and float(x[10]) > 70 for x in f)

def upright(img, rot):
    """rot: clockwise 0/90/180/270, or None to pick the turn that reads best."""
    if rot is None:
        rot = max((0, 90, 180, 270), key=lambda r: words(cv2.rotate(img, ROT[r]) if r else img))
        if rot: print(f"turned {rot} degrees clockwise so the text reads")
    return cv2.rotate(img, ROT[rot]) if rot else img

def unshadow(img):
    out = []
    for ch in cv2.split(img):
        bg = cv2.medianBlur(cv2.dilate(ch, np.ones((7, 7), np.uint8)), 21)
        out.append(cv2.normalize(255 - cv2.absdiff(ch, bg), None, 0, 255, cv2.NORM_MINMAX))
    return cv2.merge(out)

def clahe(l, c=2.0): return cv2.createCLAHE(c, (8, 8)).apply(l)

def filt(img, m):
    if m in ("color", "id"):
        l, a, b = cv2.split(cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB))
        img = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.merge([clahe(l, 1.2 if m == "id" else 2.0), a, b]), cv2.COLOR_LAB2BGR)
        k = .5
        if m == "id":  # gentle: 1-99 percentile white balance per channel
            img = cv2.merge([cv2.convertScaleAbs(c.astype(float), alpha=255 / max(hi - lo, 1), beta=-lo * 255 / max(hi - lo, 1))
                             for c, (lo, hi) in ((c, np.percentile(c, (1, 99))) for c in cv2.split(img))])
        return cv2.addWeighted(img, 1 + k, cv2.GaussianBlur(img, (0, 0), 2), -k, 0)
    if m == "shadow": return unshadow(img)
    if m == "gray": return clahe(cv2.cvtColor(unshadow(img), cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY))
    if m in ("bw", "doc"):
        g = cv2.fastNlMeansDenoising(cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY), None, 10) if m == "doc" else cv2.cvtColor(unshadow(img), cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        return cv2.adaptiveThreshold(g, 255, cv2.ADAPTIVE_THRESH_GAUSSIAN_C, cv2.THRESH_BINARY, 31, 15)
    if m == "whiteboard":
        h = cv2.cvtColor(unshadow(img), cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV); h[..., 1] = cv2.multiply(h[..., 1], 1.8)
        return cv2.cvtColor(h, cv2.COLOR_HSV2BGR)
    sys.exit(f"unknown mode {m}")

def to_pdf(pngs, out, dpi):
    with open(out, "wb") as f: f.write(img2pdf.convert(pngs, layout_fun=img2pdf.get_fixed_dpi_layout_fun((dpi, dpi))))

def c_pdf(a):
    new(a.out); txt = os.path.splitext(a.out)[0] + ".txt"; mode = "id" if a.id else "color" if a.color else "doc"
    cs = a.corners or []
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
        pngs = []
        for i, p in enumerate(a.images):
            stem = os.path.splitext(a.out)[0] + (f"-{i + 1}" if len(a.images) > 1 else "")
            img, how = flatten(load(p), stem + ".pdf", cs[i] if i < len(cs) else None, a.receipt)
            if max(img.shape[:2]) < 1600:
                f = 1600 / max(img.shape[:2]); img = cv2.resize(img, None, fx=f, fy=f, interpolation=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)
            q = f"{t}/p{i:03d}.png"; cv2.imwrite(q, filt(img, mode)); pngs.append(q)
        to_pdf(pngs, f"{t}/raw.pdf", 200)
        psm = a.psm if a.psm is not None else (3 if mode == "doc" else 11)
        subprocess.run(["ocrmypdf", "-q", "-l", a.lang, "--rotate-pages", "--deskew", "--tesseract-pagesegmode",
                        str(psm), "--optimize", "1", "--sidecar", txt, f"{t}/raw.pdf", a.out], check=True)
    print(f"wrote {a.out} and {txt}")

def c_filter(a):
    new(a.out); img = load(a.input)
    if not a.no_crop: img = flatten(img, a.out, a.corners, a.receipt)[0]
    cv2.imwrite(a.out, filt(upright(img, a.rotate), a.mode)); print(a.out)

def c_sheet(a):
    """Lay scans on A4 at real size. Items: TYPE=path, TYPE in SIZES or WxH in mm; the long side is set."""
    new(a.out); mm = 300 / 25.4; pw, ph, mg, gap = 210, 297, 12, 6; items = []
    for it in a.items:
        k, p = it.split("=", 1); img = load(p)
        L = max(SIZES[k] if k in SIZES else map(float, k.lower().split("x")))  # real long side in mm
        ih, iw = img.shape[:2]; f = L / max(ih, iw); items.append((img, iw * f, ih * f))  # keep the scan's own shape
    s = 1.0
    while True:  # shelf packing; shrink only when it overflows
        x, y, row, pos = mg, mg, 0, []
        for img, w, h in items:
            w, h = w * s, h * s
            if x + w > pw - mg + .01 and x > mg: x, y, row = mg, y + row + gap, 0
            pos.append((x, y, w, h)); x += w + gap; row = max(row, h)
        if y + row <= ph - mg or s < .3: break
        s *= .95
    if y + row > ph - mg: sys.exit("too many for one page; split them over two sheets")
    if s < 1: print(f"scaled to {s:.0%} to fit one page")
    page = np.full((int(ph * mm), int(pw * mm), 3), 255, np.uint8)
    for (img, *_), (x, y, w, h) in zip(items, pos):
        X, Y, Wp, Hp = int(x * mm), int(y * mm), int(w * mm), int(h * mm)
        page[Y:Y + Hp, X:X + Wp] = cv2.resize(img, (Wp, Hp), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
        cv2.rectangle(page, (X, Y), (X + Wp - 1, Y + Hp - 1), (200, 200, 200), 2)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
        cv2.imwrite(f"{t}/p.png", page); to_pdf([f"{t}/p.png"], a.out, 300)
    print(a.out)

def c_grid(a):
    """Copy of the photo with a labeled pixel grid, for reading corners by eye."""
    new(a.out); img = load(a.input); H, W = img.shape[:2]; st = a.step; t = max(1, max(H, W) // 800)
    for v in range(0, max(H, W), st):
        c = (0, 0, 255) if v % (st * 5) == 0 else (0, 200, 255)
        cv2.line(img, (v, 0), (v, H), c, t); cv2.line(img, (0, v), (W, v), c, t)
        for pt in ((v + 3, 25 * t), (3, v - 4)):
            cv2.putText(img, str(v), pt, 0, .6 * t, (0, 0, 0), 3 * t); cv2.putText(img, str(v), pt, 0, .6 * t, (255, 255, 255), t)
    cv2.imwrite(a.out, img); print(a.out)

def c_halves(a):
    img = load(a.input); m = img.shape[1] // 2; o = [f"{a.prefix}-1.png", f"{a.prefix}-2.png"]
    for p in o: new(p)
    cv2.imwrite(o[0], img[:, :m]); cv2.imwrite(o[1], img[:, m:]); print(*o, sep="\n")

def c_codes(a):
    from pyzbar import pyzbar
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
        ps = [a.input]
        if a.input.lower().endswith(".pdf"):
            subprocess.run(["pdftoppm", "-r", "200", "-png", a.input, f"{t}/p"], check=True)
            ps = sorted(f"{t}/{f}" for f in os.listdir(t))
        n = 0
        for p in ps:
            for c in pyzbar.decode(cv2.cvtColor(load(p), cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)):
                n += 1; print(f"{os.path.basename(p)}\t{c.type}\t{c.data.decode('utf-8', 'replace')}")
    if not n: print("no QR code or barcode found")

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); s = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
def crop_args(p): p.add_argument("--receipt", action="store_true", help="allow tall pages"); return p
p = crop_args(s.add_parser("pdf")); p.add_argument("images", nargs="+"); p.add_argument("-o", "--out", required=True)
p.add_argument("--color", action="store_true"); p.add_argument("--id", action="store_true"); p.add_argument("--lang", default="eng")
p.add_argument("--psm", type=int); p.add_argument("--corners", action="append", help="x1,y1,...,x4,y4 TL,TR,BR,BL, once per image in order"); p.set_defaults(fn=c_pdf)
p = crop_args(s.add_parser("filter")); p.add_argument("input"); p.add_argument("out"); p.add_argument("--no-crop", action="store_true")
p.add_argument("--corners"); p.add_argument("--rotate", type=int, choices=[0, 90, 180, 270])
p.add_argument("--mode", default="color", choices=["id", "color", "gray", "bw", "shadow", "whiteboard"]); p.set_defaults(fn=c_filter)
p = s.add_parser("sheet"); p.add_argument("items", nargs="+"); p.add_argument("-o", "--out", required=True); p.set_defaults(fn=c_sheet)
p = s.add_parser("grid"); p.add_argument("input"); p.add_argument("out"); p.add_argument("--step", type=int, default=100); p.set_defaults(fn=c_grid)
p = s.add_parser("halves"); p.add_argument("input"); p.add_argument("prefix"); p.set_defaults(fn=c_halves)
p = s.add_parser("codes"); p.add_argument("input"); p.set_defaults(fn=c_codes)
a = ap.parse_args(); a.fn(a)
EOF
```

## Check every crop

Each crop writes `<out>.debug.png` with the chosen corners drawn and the method that found them: `contour`, `lines`, `bright`, `grabcut`, `manual`, or `deskew` (no page found). Open it and look before you trust the scan. The crop is right when the red outline sits on the document's edges. The helper prints the corners as `x1,y1,...,x4,y4` (TL, TR, BR, BL).

If the outline is off:

1. Run `python3 ~/.file-agent/scan.py grid photo.jpg photo-grid.png` and look at it. It draws a pixel grid with labels every 100 px (`--step 50` for finer).
2. Read each corner off the grid. When a document runs past the photo's edge, use the photo's edge.
3. Rerun with `--corners x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3,x4,y4` and check the new debug image.

The auto crop accepts only shapes close to a real document (ID card, passport page, A4, Letter, or a page cut off by the frame). For a long receipt add `--receipt`. If nothing fits, ask for a retake: flat surface, darker background, all four corners in frame, no glare.

## Pick the filter

| Mode | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | IDs and passports. Gentle contrast, neutral white, light sharpening. |
| `color` | Photos and color stamps. Stronger contrast and sharpening. |
| `shadow` | Color pages with a hand or phone shadow. |
| `gray` | Text pages where color does not matter. |
| `bw` | Pages to print or fax. Pure black and white. |
| `whiteboard` | Whiteboards and marker notes. |

`python3 ~/.file-agent/scan.py filter in.jpg out.png --mode id` crops, flattens, turns the image so the text reads upright, and filters. Add `--rotate 90` (clockwise 0/90/180/270) to set the turn yourself, `--corners ...` for a manual crop, or `--no-crop` to keep the whole photo.

## Turn photos into a searchable PDF

1. Save the photos to a work folder, such as `~/files/2026-10-27/`.
2. Pick the mode: letters, forms, and receipts use the default black and white cleanup; IDs and passports add `--id`; photos and color stamps add `--color`.
3. Run `python3 ~/.file-agent/scan.py pdf p1.jpg p2.jpg -o "Type - Who - YYYY-MM-DD.pdf" --lang eng`. Photos become pages in the order given. Give `--corners` once per photo, in order, if needed.
4. Check each `<out>-N.debug.png`.
5. Read the `.txt` written next to the PDF to fill in Type, Who, and Date. Rename a copy if the first name was wrong.
6. Preview with `pdftoppm -r 60 -png -f 1 -l 1 out.pdf preview` and look at it.

## Put IDs on one copy sheet

Use this for ID front and back, or several people's IDs on one page.

1. Scan each photo with `filter --mode id` and check its debug image and result.
2. Run `python3 ~/.file-agent/scan.py sheet id1=front.png id1=back.png passport=pp.png -o "IDs - Name - YYYY-MM-DD.pdf"`. Types: `id1` (85.6 x 54 mm cards), `passport` (125 x 88 mm page), `a4`, `letter`, or `WxH` in mm. The long side is set to the real size and the scan keeps its own shape.
3. Cards go on A4 with 12 mm margins in rows. Everything shrinks evenly only when it would not fit; the helper prints the scale.
4. Preview with `pdftoppm -r 50 -png out.pdf sheet` and check that no card is cut off or overlapping.
5. To add a text layer: `ocrmypdf -l eng --tesseract-thresholding sauvola in.pdf "in - searchable.pdf"`. Keep sauvola; without it tinted cards come out blank.

To add the sheet to a form or letter, merge it as the last page: `qpdf --empty --pages letter.pdf sheet.pdf -- "letter - with IDs.pdf"`.

## Other jobs

- Two-page book spread: `python3 ~/.file-agent/scan.py halves spread.jpg book` writes `book-1.png` and `book-2.png`. Scan each half.
- A pile of different documents: group photos by document, run `pdf` once per document, name each by its own type, sender, and date, and report one line each.
- QR code or barcode: `python3 ~/.file-agent/scan.py codes photo.jpg` (PDFs too). If the value is a link, show it and ask before opening it.
- Business card: read it with `tesseract card.png - --psm 6`, then write `First Last.vcf` (vCard 3.0 with N, FN, ORG, TITLE, TEL, EMAIL) and send that file.

## Check the result

- You looked at every debug image and the final preview.
- `pdftotext out.pdf -` shows the key words.
- The original photos are unchanged.
